1. Three Real Resources, Working Together
aws_lb, aws_lb_target_group, and aws_lb_listener together form the real, complete load balancing pattern, each handling one, genuinely distinct real responsibility.
The load balancer itself receives real traffic, the target group defines where that real traffic actually goes, and the listener connects the two together.

blocks.content: Recall Security Groups, a load balancer needs its own, real, dedicated security group, allowing real, inbound traffic on the ports it actually serves.

blocks.content: 4. Target Group Health Checks
A target group's health check determines which real, actual targets are genuinely healthy, only real, healthy targets ever actually receive live traffic.
Configuring a real, correct health check path, matching an actual, real endpoint the application genuinely serves, is essential for this to work correctly.
An incorrectly configured health check can genuinely mark every, real, actually-healthy target as failed, a real, common, confusing source of an outage.
This real, practical detail deserves careful, deliberate attention, it directly determines whether real traffic ever successfully reaches an application at all.

6. Recap: create_before_destroy, Applied Here
Recall create_before_destroy, already covered, applied here directly, a real, zero-downtime replacement pattern for the actual, live instances behind this load balancer.
New, real instances join the target group, and pass their real health check, before old ones are ever actually removed from real, live rotation.

blocks.content: 8. A Real, Common Mistake
Forgetting to configure a real, correct health check path is a real, common mistake, causing a real, live load balancer to mark genuinely healthy targets as failed.
This often happens because the default, real health check path does not actually match a specific, real application's own, genuine health endpoint.
The honest fix is explicitly, deliberately confirming the real health check path matches an actual, live, working endpoint the application genuinely serves.
This mistake is worth testing directly, hitting the real health check path manually, before ever relying on it in a real, live, production deployment.

blocks.content: A single, real load balancer can genuinely route different, real paths or hostnames to different target groups, using listener rules beyond the simple default action.
This lets one, real load balancer genuinely serve several, distinct applications, /api routed to one target group, /app routed to another, real, separate one.
This is a real, practical cost and management optimization, avoiding a real, separate load balancer for every single application a team genuinely runs.
This connects directly to the target group concept already covered, several real target groups, one shared, real load balancer in front.
